theory.intro: Rainfall depth is measured in millimetres by a rain gauge. The volume of rain that falls on a piece of land is $V=Ah$, where $A$ is the area of the land and $h$ is the depth of rain. Convert the depth to metres first.
facts: $V=Ah$, where $V$ is the volume of rain, $A$ is the area of land and $h$ is the depth of rain.
The depth is given in millimetres, so divide by $1000$ to get metres: $25$ mm $=0.025$ m.
With $A$ in square metres and $h$ in metres, $V$ comes out in cubic metres.
Read the unit the question asks for — cubic metres, litres, kilolitres or megalitres — and convert at the very end.
If a stated percentage of the rain is lost to runoff or overflow, multiply the volume by the fraction that is actually collected.
Multiplying the area by the depth in millimetres, without converting, gives an answer $1000$ times too large.
steps: Convert the depth of rain from millimetres to metres
Find the area of the land or roof in square metres
Multiply to get $V=Ah$ in cubic metres, then convert to the unit asked for

foundation.question_text: A flat roof has an area of $150\text{ m}^{2}$. During a storm, $25$ mm of rain falls on it. Find the volume of water that falls on the roof, in cubic metres.

The surface of a lake has an area of $480\,000\text{ m}^{2}$. An average of $8$ mm of rain falls on the lake. Find the increase in the volume of water, in cubic metres. Ignore any runoff from the surrounding land.
A shed roof has an area of $220\text{ m}^{2}$. If $12$ mm of rain falls on it, how many litres of water fall on the roof?
A paddock has an area of $25\,000\text{ m}^{2}$. During a week, $30$ mm of rain falls on it. Find the volume of rainfall, in kilolitres.
A car park has an area of $1800\text{ m}^{2}$. In one afternoon, $45$ mm of rain falls on it. Find the volume of rainfall, in kilolitres.
A farm dam has a surface area of $64\,000\text{ m}^{2}$. If $15$ mm of rain falls on it, find the increase in the volume of water, in megalitres.
A rectangular shed roof measures $18$ m by $9$ m. During a storm $6$ mm of rain falls on it. Find the volume of water collected from the roof, in litres.

development.question_text: A floor plan gives a rectangular garage roof as $7200$ mm by $6000$ mm. During a storm $20$ mm of rain falls on it. Find the volume of water that falls on the roof, in kilolitres.

A house roof has an area of $180\text{ m}^{2}$. The average annual rainfall in the area is $650$ mm, but $15\%$ of the rain is lost to leaks and overflow. How much water is collected in a year, in kilolitres?
During a storm $32$ mm of rain falls on a roof of area $95\text{ m}^{2}$, and $90\%$ of it reaches the tank. Find the volume of water that reaches the tank, in litres.
A storm delivers $9.6\text{ m}^{3}$ of water onto a flat roof, and the rain gauge recorded $16$ mm of rain. Find the area of the roof, in square metres.
A paddock of area $12\,000\text{ m}^{2}$ received $2400$ kL of rain during one month. Find the depth of rain that fell, in millimetres.
A reservoir has a surface area of $2.4\text{ km}^{2}$. If $18$ mm of rain falls on it, find the increase in the volume of water, in megalitres.
A rectangular carport roof measures $6.4$ m by $3.5$ m. During a storm $28$ mm of rain falls on it. Find the volume of water that falls on the roof, in litres.

mastery.question_text: All the rain falling on a roof of area $240\text{ m}^{2}$ is piped into a rectangular tank whose base measures $2.5$ m by $1.6$ m. During a storm $12$ mm of rain falls. By how many centimetres does the water level in the tank rise?

A household roof has an area of $200\text{ m}^{2}$ and the average annual rainfall is $750$ mm, of which $10\%$ is lost to overflow. Town water costs $\$2.40$ per kilolitre. How much would the household save in a year by using the tank water instead of town water?
A tank collected $4500$ L of water from a shed roof of area $125\text{ m}^{2}$, with none of the rain lost. Find the depth of rain that fell, in millimetres.
